LESSON: READING 9.2.1 EXTENSIVE READING: DIALOGUES

Grade: Grade 6
Subject: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
Strand: Strand 9
Topic 9.2: Reading 9.2.1 Extensive Reading: Dialogues

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Reading 9.2.1 Extensive Reading: Dialogues. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: How can we extract information from a text?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify vocabulary from a text for information
2. respond to direct and inferential questions for comprehension
3. appreciate the importance of reading indigenous texts for enjoyment

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: READING 9.2.1 EXTENSIVE READING: DIALOGUES
Subject: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES · Grade: Grade 6
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Reading 9.2.1 Extensive Reading: Dialogues helps you succeed in INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: READING 9.2.1 EXTENSIVE READING: DIALOGUES
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Identify vocabulary from a text for information

What this means
In this part you learn to identify vocabulary from a text for information. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify vocabulary from a text for information.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Reading 9.2.1 Extensive Reading: Dialogues”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify vocabulary from a text for information. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Respond to direct and inferential questions for comprehension

What this means
In this part you learn to respond to direct and inferential questions for comprehension. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: respond to direct and inferential questions for comprehension.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Reading 9.2.1 Extensive Reading: Dialogues to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can respond to direct and inferential questions for comprehension. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Appreciate the importance of reading indigenous texts for enjoyment

What this means
In this part you learn to appreciate the importance of reading indigenous texts for enjoyment. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: appreciate the importance of reading indigenous texts for enjoyment.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model writing: Write 5 neat sentences using new words from this lesson.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can appreciate the importance of reading indigenous texts for enjoyment. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Reading 9.2.1 Extensive Reading: Dialogues is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Reading 9.2.1 Extensive Reading: Dialogues”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: identify vocabulary from a text for information)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Reading 9.2.1 Extensive Reading: Dialogues to a partner. (skill: respond to direct and inferential questions for comprehension)

Example 3: Write 5 neat sentences using new words from this lesson. (skill: appreciate the importance of reading indigenous texts for enjoyment)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Reading 9.2.1 Extensive Reading: Dialogues to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: identify vocabulary from a text for information.
3. Practise this skill: respond to direct and inferential questions for comprehension.
4. Practise this skill: appreciate the importance of reading indigenous texts for enjoyment.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Reading 9.2.1 Extensive Reading: Dialogues from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Reading 9.2.1 Extensive Reading: Dialogues: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 6 learner study Reading 9.2.1 Extensive Reading: Dialogues?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How can we extract information from a text?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Reading 9.2.1 Extensive Reading: Dialogues means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: identify vocabulary from a text for information.
5. Be able to: respond to direct and inferential questions for comprehension.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
